source_name: EKR – Elektronikus Közbeszerzési Rendszer (public procedure search)
why_relevant: Hungary's mandatory end-to-end e-procurement platform. Every in-scope procedure (incl. bank/state-owned buyers acting as contracting authorities) is run here; the public procedure list exposes procedure subject, contracting authority and status, which is the entry point to ATM/POS/kiosk/card-personalisation tenders and their result stages.

source_name: EKR – Eredménytájékoztató hirdetmények (contract award notice data download)
why_relevant: The single most on-point page for this cell: award-result notices ('eredménytájékoztató') state the winning bidder (nyertes ajánlattevő) and contract value — the explicit vendor-buyer pair. Appears to offer bulk/structured download rather than notice-by-notice reading.

source_name: EKR Publikus Szerződéstár (public contract register)
why_relevant: Register of concluded public contracts and their modifications. Gives contract text/metadata beyond the award notice — duration, scope, amendments and extensions — which is what tells you when an ATM-fleet or POS contract actually comes up for rebid.

source_name: Közbeszerzési Értesítő (Official Journal of the Public Procurement Authority)
why_relevant: The official gazette carrying all domestic (below-EU-threshold and national) procurement notices, published every working day and freely available. Below-threshold notices matter because many single-bank ATM/POS/kiosk lots never reach the TED threshold.

source_name: Közbeszerzési Hatóság – Hirdetmény kereső (notice search)
why_relevant: Queryable index over the Értesítő notices — the practical way to retrieve historical ATM/POS/kiosk notices by keyword, CPV and contracting authority rather than reading daily issues.

source_name: KBA – Közbeszerzési Adatbázis (central procurement database)
why_relevant: Central registry storing procedure- and authority-level data and documents (plans, statements, contracts). Useful for building the buyer-side actor map: which banks/state bodies procure payment tech and on what cycle.

source_name: CoRe Publikus Kereső (Közbeszerzési Hatóság core public search)
why_relevant: Newer unified public search over the Authority's registries; likely the most complete single query surface across notices, contracts and authorities.

source_name: Közbeszerzési Döntőbizottság – határozatok (review board decisions)
why_relevant: Remedy decisions name BOTH the winner and the challenging losing bidders, quote technical specifications, prices and evaluation scores — the richest public source on competitor positioning and on how ATM/POS specs are written. Also flags contested or annulled awards that a naive award-notice feed would record as settled.

source_name: KEF Központosított Közbeszerzési Portál (kozbeszerzes.gov.hu)
why_relevant: The central purchasing body (Közbeszerzési és Ellátási Főigazgatóság) runs framework agreements ('keretmegállapodás') for kiemelt termékek including IT and telecom. Vendors admitted to a KEF framework can supply the whole central-government estate without a fresh open tender — so the framework roster is a de facto competitor whitelist and a critical rebid clock.

source_name: TED – Tenders Electronic Daily (Hungary, advanced search + bulk data)
source_subtype: EU official journal supplement / open dataset
why_relevant: All above-EU-threshold Hungarian notices, including contract-award notices, are duplicated here in structured, machine-readable form with CPV codes and winner records. Best machine-readable backbone; Hungarian-language notice text is also available (ted.europa.eu/hu/notice/...).

source_name: Opentender.eu – Hungary (Government Transparency Institute)
why_relevant: Cleans and merges TED with the Hungarian national portal so that BELOW-threshold contracts are included, and normalises supplier names — which solves the biggest analytical problem in this cell (the same vendor appearing under many spellings/entity forms). Good for market-share and rebid-cycle analytics.

source_name: K-Monitor adatbázis (public-money watchdog, tagged by organisation)
why_relevant: NGO-curated index of press articles and documents tagged by contracting authority and company (e.g. a dedicated KEF tag). Excellent pointer layer: surfaces the deals that got journalistic scrutiny, and thereby names actors and contract nicknames you can then look up in the primary registers.

source_name: Tender-értesítő (kozbeszerzes figyelő + winner lists + API)
why_relevant: Commercial monitoring service that explicitly markets winner lists ('nyertesek') for competitor study and offers an API for workflow integration — i.e. a ready-made structured feed over the same notices, plus a usable public CPV code reference list.

source_name: KHF – Közbeszerzési Hirdetmény Figyelő
why_relevant: Aggregates Hungarian Értesítő + TED + other HU sources into one keyword-monitored feed and publishes free annual procurement statistics; also hosts a downloadable CPV code list useful for building the collection filter.

source_name: TenderMonitor / Napitender / InnoTender (HU tender-alert cluster)
why_relevant: Secondary alerting layer over the same statutory notices. Value is redundancy and early notification rather than unique content; also a pointer to which sectors/keywords the local market itself treats as one category.

source_name: Magyar Posta Zrt. – Beszerzések, pályázatok (buyer-side procurement page)
why_relevant: Magyar Posta is one of the largest HU buyers of self-service kiosks, cash-handling and counter payment technology (its 400-unit self-service kiosk programme surfaced in the Értesítő). Buyer-side pages often carry documentation and results that are easier to read than the gazette version.

source_name: MÁV-csoport – Közbeszerzés (rail buyer: ticket vending machines, card acceptance)
why_relevant: Adjacent but in-scope buyer for unattended payment: jegykiadó automata (ticket vending machines) with card acceptance, on-board POS, and their maintenance. Same vendor pool as banking self-service; contracts are large and on multi-year rebid cycles.

source_name: Diákhitel Központ – Közbeszerzésekkel kapcsolatos közzétételek
why_relevant: Example of a state-owned financial institution publishing its own procurement disclosures and contracts (card issuance, payment processing, IT). Template for the wider class of state-owned financial buyers whose disclosure pages must each be enumerated.

source_name: Magyar Nemzeti Bank – procurement notices in the Értesítő (banknote processing / cash-handling machines)
source_subtype: central-bank contracting authority notices + approved-equipment register
why_relevant: The central bank tenders banknote-processing machines and their maintenance; the notice found is a concrete worked example of the record type this cell targets (buyer, subject, maintenance service). MNB also publishes the list of tested/approved banknote and coin authentication machines, which doubles as a vendor roster.

source_name: Közbeszerzési Hatóság – Statisztika (procurement statistics portal)
why_relevant: Aggregate market sizing and procedure-type distribution — useful denominators for judging whether a vendor's award count is meaningful, and for detecting shifts toward negotiated/in-house awards that would hide the vendor-buyer pair.

source_name: Ertesítő Plusz (Közbeszerzési Hatóság professional journal)
why_relevant: The Authority's expert commentary journal explains framework-agreement mechanics, in-house exemptions and evaluation practice — the interpretive layer that tells you why certain payment-tech contracts never appear as open tenders.

source_name: Nemzeti Jogszabálytár / Jogtár – Kbt. and 424/2017 (XII.19.) Korm. rendelet on e-procurement
why_relevant: Defines what MUST be published, where, in what form and within what deadline — i.e. the legal guarantee behind this whole cell, plus the exemptions (in-house, defence/security, central-bank secrecy) that predict the blind spots in the award record.

source_name: TED — Tenders Electronic Daily (EU official procurement journal, EN interface)
why_relevant: Above-threshold Hungarian public-sector and state-owned-bank contracts must be published EU-wide here. Contract award notices name the winning vendor, contract value, duration and CPV subject matter — the single richest deterministic source for HU banking/payments vendor and competitor wins.

source_name: TED — Hungarian-language interface (TED – Uniós tenderek, a Hivatalos Lap kiegészítése)
why_relevant: Same corpus as TED EN but rendered in Hungarian; Hungarian notice text carries the original procuring-entity names, lot descriptions and product wording (e.g. 'bankkártya elfogadás', 'önkiszolgáló kioszk') that the EN translation flattens. Mandatory for local-language matching of vendor/product terms.

source_name: TED Search API (docs.ted.europa.eu / api.ted.europa.eu)
why_relevant: Machine-readable expert-query access to the whole TED corpus, no authentication required for search according to the docs. This is the collection backbone for the whole cell: deterministic CPV + country + notice-type filters, repeatable on a schedule.

source_name: TED XML bulk download (daily/monthly packages)
why_relevant: Full historical archive of notices in XML, including award history that national portals purge. Enables retrospective vendor-share reconstruction for Hungarian banking/payments CPVs over many years without hammering the search API.

source_name: TED CPV vocabulary reference (Fő és kiegészítő közös közbeszerzési szójegyzék)
why_relevant: Authoritative bilingual CPV code list; gives the exact Hungarian label for each code so queries and downstream classification use the official term rather than a guess. Essential to build the checklist-free CPV slice for this cell.

source_name: EU Open Data Portal — TED dataset (data.europa.eu)
why_relevant: Curated CSV/XML redistributions of TED with long historical coverage, easier to load into analysis than raw notice XML. Useful as a cross-check and for quick country+CPV aggregate counts.
